key_highlights: ASX treads water amid oil price spike and Fed meeting focus; 10-year US yield hits 5% pressuring global equities
Iron ore crash confirmed, posing direct headwind to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX revenue outlook
Strategic metals rally: tin-tungsten (Critica), battery-grade graphite (Sarytogan), and Pentagon-linked metal producer up 43% signal rotation into critical minerals
ANZ.AX completes 3,500-job cut but restructuring plan faces long execution path; housing auction market shows no spring bounce
Houthi seizure of Red Sea islands drives oil spike, pressuring fuel prices and Albanese government on second excise cut
Global AI rotation: Nvidia/Broadcom tumble on Anthropic warnings; capital flows into UK and defensive names
Australia nears energy inflection point; private hospital operator collapses into division; major caravan manufacturer shuts

sectors.trend: Iron ore crash confirmed as China demand weakens; however, critical minerals (tin, tungsten, graphite, gold) attract capital rotation. Strategic metal producer up 43% on Pentagon deals signals defence-driven demand.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore decline. Small-cap miners (Critica, Sarytogan, PLC Resources, Forrestania) benefit from critical-minerals and gold rotation. Diversified miners with copper/gold exposure relatively insulated.

sectors.trend: ANZ.AX post-restructuring (3,500 jobs cut) faces execution risk; housing market soft with no auction bounce and falling prices. 10-year yield at 5% pressures bond portfolios and mortgage demand.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX face NIM compression risk if RBA holds rates amid weak housing. Credit quality concerns in residential mortgage book. REITs (GPW.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by higher discount rates.

sectors.trend: Oil spike on Houthi Red Sea escalation; fuel price blowout pressures Australian consumers and government. Australia nears energy inflection point (renewables transition). YPF $24B LNG project signals global LNG demand.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX benefit from oil spike. BHP.AX LNG division supported. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX) face input cost pressure. Renewable energy names gain on inflection narrative.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator collapses into division; SA Health data breach; bird flu in endangered sea lions. Sector under stress from operational and regulatory pressures.
sectors.implications: Private hospital operators (IAG.AX-linked, ADF.AX) face consolidation risk. CSL.AX relatively insulated as global biotech. Public health funding scrutiny may increase.

sectors.trend: Caravan manufacturer shuts; fuel costs squeeze discretionary spend. Global AI rotation away from mega-cap chips (Nvidia, Broadcom) into UK and defensive names. Anthropic AI warnings spook tech.
sectors.implications: Consumer discretionary (WBC.AX retail, CAR.AX) under pressure. ASX tech (W1.AX, XRO.AX) limited direct exposure but sentiment spillover from global AI selloff. Defensive consumer staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX) preferred.

key_themes: Iron ore crash vs critical minerals rotation
Fed rate hike risk and 5% 10-year yield global repricing
Red Sea / Houthi geopolitical oil risk
AI sector global de-rating and capital rotation
Immigration policy uncertainty and productivity debate

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weightings; rotate into gold and critical-minerals exposure
Shorten duration in fixed income; favour floating-rate and short-dated bonds; hedge AUD/USD

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Red Sea shipping disruption / oil spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge fuel-cost exposure; favour energy producers (WDS.AX, WLE.AX); monitor freight indices
Underweight REITs and home-loan-heavy banks; monitor auction clearance rates and RBA policy
Avoid chasing AI momentum; favour defensive and dividend-paying ASX names
Monitor construction and labour-intensive sectors; watch RBA commentary on migration-driven demand

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight critical minerals and gold miners
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore crash drives rotation into strategic metals; Pentagon deals and battery-grade graphite demand support structural upside

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy producers on oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Houthi Red Sea escalation supports oil prices; Australian energy names benefit from higher realised prices
Fuel cost blowout and AI uncertainty favour low-beta, dividend-paying staples

defensive_moves.rationale: Confirmed iron ore crash with China demand weakness; FMG.AX and RIO.AX most exposed

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge rate risk and shorten bond duration
defensive_moves.rationale: 10-year yield at 5% and Fed hike risk pressure long-duration assets and REITs
3,500-job cut complete but execution plan long; housing softness pressures NIM and credit

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely range-bound to modestly lower over 1–3 months. Oil spike supports energy but iron ore crash and global AI de-rating cap upside. Fed meeting and 5% 10-year yield create volatility. Fuel excise cut debate adds political noise. Expect sector rotation from mega-cap miners into critical minerals and defensives.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if iron ore stabilises and Australia's energy transition delivers. Critical minerals and gold offer structural tailwinds. Housing market softening may prompt RBA easing, supporting financials and REITs later in cycle. Productivity vs immigration debate will shape GDP trajectory.

Iron ore price floor and China stimulus response
RBA cash rate decision and housing data
Red Sea shipping normalisation or escalation
Australian energy policy / renewables investment pipeline
Immigration policy finalisation and productivity data

RBA cash rate and CPI print
ANZ.AX restructuring progress and NIM trends
Critical minerals: tin, tungsten, graphite, gold prices
